posts:
Pat Bagley’s latest cartoon tackles our turbulent times as the Salt Lake Tribune removes paywalls to combat rising misinformation.
Evidence: Free access, Nonprofit funding, Local journalism
#Aletheia #Journalism

The Salt Lake Tribune announced that its site is now completely free to access, relying on donations to ensure trustworthy news reaches everyone.
Stated Judgement: (+0.80, +0.90) — Greater Good

Operating as a nonprofit newsroom, the Tribune successfully maintains open public access through reader donations and community grants.
Resulting Judgement: (+0.78, +0.88) — Greater Good

Verdict: PASS — Small Fall from Grace.
Open nonprofit funding successfully preserves local accountability without paywalls.

Integrity: Trustworthy (Hypocrisy: 1.05, z: 0)

Sub-Audits Breakdown:
- Access Model: PASS (+0.8, +0.9) — Eliminates paywalls effectively.
- Nonprofit Model: PASS (+0.75, +0.85) — Relies on genuine community support.
The Salt Lake Tribune eliminated its subscription paywall to keep independent journalism accessible in an era of rising misinformation and AI-generated content.

The Bright Side:
Removing paywalls empowers lower-income communities to access vital local reporting and satirical commentary without financial barriers.

The Breakdown & Plane Error:
Evaluating this story requires looking at WHO funds public goods (metaphysical) versus WHERE paywalls stand (physical).

Social Physics Analysis:
By replacing extractive paywalls with transparent community donations, the Tribune executes a Smart Altruistic Loop, replacing conflict with open civic empowerment.

The Trajectory: The Path of Small Fall from Grace.
When you map open access against community funding, it plots a direct trajectory toward Grace. Altruistic alignment yields sustainable public trust.

The Unavoidable Truth: Free public news requires honest community support to survive.

The Unavoidable Lie: Quality journalism can persist indefinitely without any financial backing.

Alethekanon:
Removing financial barriers to local news safeguards public knowledge against ideological echo chambers.

Awwthekanon:
It is deeply heartwarming to see a local newspaper choose community access over profit, trusting readers to keep the truth alive together.

Brothekanon:
Pretty awesome move by the Trib to drop the paywall. Good journalism should be for everybody, not just whoever can afford a monthly sub.

Spirithekanon:
"The truly rich give freely of what they know and have." Tao Te Ching 81 PASS (Spiritual Vector)
True wealth and knowledge multiply when shared openly without restrictive barriers.

Actual Article Body:
Pat Bagley | Apocalypse Now-ish

Thanks for reading this story from The Tribune. As CEO & Executive Editor, I am proud to lead our team of journalists as they tell the stories others can’t – or won’t.

Cartoonist Pat Bagley is a Pulitzer Prize finalist who has worked for The Tribune for more than 45 years, publishing more than 6,000 cartoons.

You can support Pat’s legacy of independent editorial cartooning here, by making a donation to our nonprofit newsroom.

Tribune reporters are dedicated to shining a light on how Utah works, from daily reporting that empowers Utahns to make informed decisions about their communities to investigative projects on the power structures in this state.

The critical work we do wouldn’t be possible without people like you – individuals who understand the power of local, independent journalism.

When you support the nonprofit Salt Lake Tribune, you’re doing more than making a donation: you’re investing in a future where transparency, accountability, and community thrive.

Join us in this work.

Give today.

(Rick Egan | The Salt Lake Tribune) Lauren Gustus, executive editor of The Salt Lake Tribune.

sltrib.com is now free to access — no subscription required. We made this decision because we believe access to trustworthy, independent news shouldn’t depend on what you can afford — especially as misinformation and AI-generated content continue to rise.

Free to read doesn’t mean free to produce. Our reporters show up every day to ask hard questions and hold powerful institutions to account. That work takes resources. As a nonprofit newsroom, we rely on support from people who believe it matters. Make a donation today to fund local news that serves Utah communities.

You can help us bring more local news to more communities today.

Sponsored: American Cancer Society hosts Utah’s largest breast cancer walk.
